narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: Dance historian or classical ballet master
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The era began in the early 19th century, influenced by Romanticism in Europe.
It is traditionally dated from 1815 to 1870, with the 1832 premiere of La Sylphide in Paris serving as a primary catalyst.
on_screen: Map: France · Europe

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The ballets focused on the dichotomy between the real world and the spiritual realm.
Plots frequently involved spirit women who enslaved the hearts of mortal men.
Today it is a historical tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers utilized early pointe work to create an ethereal, floating effect.
The movement style is characterized by soft, rounded arms, a forward tilt of the upper body, and elaborate leg movements.
Watch for Pointe work.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Early ballets often used pastiche music, but the era evolved to include specially written scores.
Adolphe Adam introduced the leitmotif, and composers like Léo Delibes later contributed to the genre's musical sophistication.
Listen for the Orchestra, Harp.
The music evolved from simple, melodic pastiche to more structured compositions using leitmotifs to represent characters and emotions.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The Romantic tutu, a long, white, multi-layered tulle skirt, is the signature costume.
Settings often featured supernatural, moonlit landscapes, enhanced by the introduction of gas lighting.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Marie Taglioni, Carlotta Grisi, Lucille Grahn, Fanny Cerrito, Pauline Leroux, Fanny Elssler, and choreographers like Jules Perrot and Filippo Taglioni.
While centered in Paris and London, the style spread across Europe.
Succeeded the 'ballet d'action' of the 18th century and preceded the 'grand ballet' of the late 19th century.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Romantic ballet (France). Instruments: Orchestra, Harp. Mood: lyrical, mysterious, ethereal. It should sound like this: The music evolved from simple, melodic pastiche to more structured compositions using leitmotifs to represent characters and emotions. tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.

wardrobe.policy: neutral dress with a respectful nod (palette and fabric only): the sources describe sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire, or the dance is sacred

no caricature, no exaggeration, no mixing of regions or eras
a culture bearer reviews the wardrobe before production; the review is recorded in the pack
